results.question: What is the main purpose of separating the screening and matching actions in the Hiring-Assistant system?
results.ground_truth_answer: To decouple screening and matching, allowing them to be handled as separate processes.
results.retrieved_answer: The goal is to decouple the two steps so that **screening can run continuously and independently of matching**, letting hiring teams review and clean the candidate pool (e.g., flag missing data, suspect candidates) at any time, while **matching is triggered later—only after the SRF is ready (closed to applications, reaches a target number of candidates, or is manually started).** This separation gives greater control, flexibility, and auditability over when and how candidates are scored and advanced.

Feature – Resume screening

Currently the Hiring-Assistant (HA) system does the screening and matching together – we want it to be 2 separate processes.

Purpose of this process:

Decouple Screening and Matching actions on the system.

Normally, during the SRF life-cycle, matching is only requested/initiated after the srf has been posted for a few pre-set numbers of days.

This is controlled by the Hiring Manager based on many criterias like

The SRF has accumulated a certain number of active/prospective candidates.

Candidate matching may only begin after the SRF is closed to applications so that we have a closed set of candidates to review.

Screening process can be an ongoing user-initiated and/or scheduled process during the full period SRF has been active/open to application.

The data-view created, will allow TA users to review suspect-list candidates, incomplete applications (missing-data status), Candidate_ experience, etc. and select them for Scoring/Candidate matching Phase.

How this should work:

This process would be initiated via 2 methods:

User triggered, from HA platform taking a valid SRF id as input.

Or A scheduled daily process will run on HA for all SRFs on ORC, which are currently Active for candidates to apply for.

User Work-Flow (User-initiated Screening)

After SRF creation on ORC, User will log into the HA platform.

User go to SRF-Details page and will enter the SRF ID (valid on ORC) on the screen to initiate the process.

HA system calls ORC get-SRF API to get specific SRF details, Add/update the details on SRF-Details table and display on the screen for user to review. (below)

SRF-ID

SRF-Title

SRF-Status

HA-Process-Status, set to ‘Initiated by User-ID’, if new. Get from SRF-Details table, if already exists.

ORC-Fetch-Date, set to system date-time or ORC call.

(other SRF fields, if requested on BRD)

> Approved -> tagged-to-TA/TSC -> ... etc.

After SRF has passed the Approved state;

HM adds/selects Question-set for AI Interview from AI-generated/user input List for specific Job-Role requirement.Flow continues with SRF ‘Tagged to TA’:

For each SRF tagged to TA:

User can view AI-recommended candidates, from the Internal Talent Pool consisting of previously Screened candidates who are not currently tagged to any SRFs.

HA-Platform users (TA team) can view the AI- recommended candidate list and tag them to this SRF individually or as a whole, and mark them as ‘Ready for Scoring’.

TA team can choose to publish the SRF to identified channels to allow candidates to apply directly on Zensar-Careers or via 3rd party channels.

This recommended candidate list will grow, as newer candidates apply or are sourced from 3rd party to the system.

TA team can decide to close the SRF to new application, once they are satisfied with the number of candidate applications tagged for the SRF. This will mark the SRF as ‘Shortlisting in progress / Closed to new application’.

TA team can decide to Score the list of candidates tagged to an SRF, before or after closing the SRF for new candidate applications and view/download and action on the Scored list of candidates.

TA team can select individual scored candidates (or multiple) and mark them as

Either ‘Shortlisted’.

Or ‘Not-Taken-Forward’.

On being shortlisted, system will trigger email notifications to candidate to ‘Apply’ within a specific date-range.

If Candidate applies within the date-range, then the process moves forward, and the Candidate is locked with ‘Application in progress’ status for the tagged SRF.

If no apply is registered for the date range; system will mark the candidate as ‘Not-interested’ for the tagged SRF.

Internal Talent pool –

All candidates will be screened at the point of inception.

If candidate sourced directly or via 3rd party, for an SRF, they will be tagged to that SRF in the Talent Pool.

Product Module Design:

Based on the BRD, I have broken down the Product platform into specific functional modules in sequence of build requirement.

HM/TA portal – UI/UX

SRF Creation (with real-time AI recommendations)

JD optimization – AI module

JD publishing – Internal/External

Talent-Pool Management

Candidate Sourcing – Direct/Internal/External

Candidate Screening – AI module

Candidate Scoring (matching to SRF) – AI module with dynamic weightage selection.

Candidate Portal – UI/UX

AI-Assessment – Create questionnaire

AI-Assessment – MCQ/subjective with support for code writing etc.

SRF Status updates and Dashboard

Candidate Status updates and Dashboard

Communication and notifications – template and AI driven

Interview scheduling – AI driven

Interview Panel management

Dashboard views and extracts

Logging and event management

Flow starts with SRF Creation:  - Module A – Job Description/SRF Creation:

The above flow indicates a Real-time integration of AI module to the user-interface, for AI-driven skill recommendations and setup Assessment questions for the SRF, which is not possible in ORC.

Based on Discussion on 23rd June 2025 -

Module A – Job Description/SRF Creation:

SRF creation to be done wholly on the new HA Platform with AI features.

All User actions, related to flows will be verified and tracked with timestamps; which can be used for audits latter on.

After setting up the SRF, Hiring Manager (HM) will then be able to either

'Cancel’ it, if required.

Or

mark it as ‘Fulfilled Internally’ and ‘Closed’.

Or

‘Tagged to TA’ for further actions.

HM / User, can view all SRFs created by them – edit their status to previous stage or next stage based on their requirements.

Like New -> pending Approval -> Approved -> tagged-to-TA/TSC -> ... etc.

After SRF has passed the Approved state;

HM adds/selects Question-set for AI Interview from AI-generated/user input List for specific Job-Role requirement.

results.question: When is candidate matching typically initiated according to the SRF life-cycle?
results.ground_truth_answer: After the SRF has been posted for a few preset number of days and based on criteria such as accumulated candidates or when the SRF is closed to applications.
results.retrieved_answer: Candidate matching is normally started **after the SRF has been open for the preset posting period (or after it’s closed to new applications), so that a closed set of candidates can be reviewed.**

results.question: What are the two ways the screening process can be initiated?
results.ground_truth_answer: User-triggered from the HA platform with a valid SRF ID, or a scheduled daily process for all active SRFs.
results.retrieved_answer:
The screening can be started in two ways:

1. **User‑initiated screening** – the user clicks the “Fetch Candidate List” (or enters an SRF‑ID) on the HA platform, which calls ORC and runs the screening process for that SRF.

2. **Scheduled (automated) screening** – a scheduled job runs at a predefined time/frequency, pulls all active SRFs from ORC and automatically invokes the screening process for each SRF.

results.question: What values can the Candidate_Status field have after screening, and what do they indicate?
results.ground_truth_answer: 'Ready for matching' if all relevant data is available; 'Missing_Data' if required data is absent.
results.retrieved_answer:
**Candidate_Status values that are set **by the screening step** (and what each value means)**  

| Value | When it is applied | What it indicates |
|-------|-------------------|-------------------|
| **Ready for Matching** | All required data (resume, primary/secondary skills, experience, etc.) is present after the screen. | The record is complete and can be queued for the matching engine. |
| **Missing_Data** | One or more mandatory fields (e.g., resume, email, phone, primary‑skill) could not be retrieved from ORC. | The candidate needs additional information before it can be considered for matching. |
| **Queue for Matching** | User has manually moved a “Ready for Matching” record (or a record that has just been re‑screened) to the matching work‑list. | The candidate is now in the work‑queue awaiting the matching run. |
| **Removed from Matching** | User explicitly removes a candidate from the matching work‑list (e.g., after a manual review). | The candidate will be ignored by the next matching run. |
| **Score Assigned** | The matching engine has finished scoring the candidate (AI inference on the resume). | The candidate now has a total score, positives/negatives, AI comments, etc., and is ready for the next step (short‑listing, offer, etc.). |
| **Rejected** *(post‑screening)* | Screening flagged the candidate as a suspect/blocked name **or** the user manually rejects after a later interview round. | The candidate is removed from the pipeline and a “rejection” email is sent; the profile is kept only in the talent pool. |
| **Selected for BGV** *(after later interview steps)* | After interview rounds the candidate is marked as selected and moves into background‑verification. | Not a direct screening status, but shows the candidate has progressed beyond screening. |

**In short:** Immediately after the screening job runs a candidate can only be **“Ready for Matching”** (complete data) or **“Missing_Data”** (incomplete data). Subsequent user actions or automated processes can change the field to **“Queue for Matching,” “Removed from Matching,” “Score Assigned,”** and later **“Rejected”** or **“Selected for BGV.”** Each value tells the platform and the recruiter whether the record is ready to be matched, needs more information, is in the matching queue, has been excluded, has been scored, or has moved out of the screening flow.
